items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: So a guy I played ball with, Joe Lotempio, he started at Baker Hall now in Buffalo

ctx.x: Yeah. So you know that those guys would go for Sunday. They’d say, “You’ve got to make a stop at Rochester, the Mangione family will take good care of you.” So she said — I said, “well let me know something about them. Bring their scrapbook and everything else.” The first concert I ever did was the Mangione brothers. 196 — it was probably ’65 or maybe late ’64. I don’t have any posters of it, but that was the first one I did. And that was the beginning of me putting on concerts and eventually doing things where I…

that time, and guys like Dave Roll and Bobby Weiss and those guys, “How come you didn’t play with the ABA?” They didn’t have an ABA. And it turns out I couldn’t go to the college. I had a scholarship from all of them and I wanted to go to McGill, because I spoke a little French, because to me that was as European as you can get, you know, up there in Ottawa. And they didn’t have any of it. So I had a scholarship there and then right before I was going to start I get this letter. Now this is the summer of ’65,…

he says, “I told them, I don’t want to do it anymore.” So anyway, so I did all kinds of teaching there. And then I came for my master’s and Tallmadge asked me to do review classes in 1969 in the library. And they loved what I was doing.
